html:
A Hong Kong and American martial artist and film star who made kung fu films popular around the world.

He was born in San Francisco while his father, a Cantonese opera singer, was on tour, and grew up in Hong Kong, where he acted in films as a child. He studied the Wing Chun style of kung fu under Ip Man. At 18 he was sent to the United States, studied philosophy and opened martial arts schools, teaching non Chinese students when many masters would not. He founded his own approach, Jeet Kune Do, which threw out fixed forms and took whatever worked from many styles, drawing on Zen and Taoism.

American television gave him only side roles, so he went back to Hong Kong. His films there, such as The Big Boss and Fist of Fury, broke box office records. Enter the Dragon, made with Hollywood, came out days after his sudden death at 32 from swelling of the brain. He changed how Asian men were shown in Hollywood and on screen everywhere, and helped bring Asian martial arts to the West.
sum: A Hong Kong and American martial artist and film star who made kung fu films popular around the world.
